title: Tokenized Vaults

strong.description: Contract's inheritance list (Slither Contract.inheritance / immediate bases) includes an interface named IERC4626 (or IERC-4626/IERC_4626 spelling variants).
Contract's inheritance list includes a base contract literally named ERC4626 (the common pattern for both OpenZeppelin's and Solmate's reference implementations, and any project-local copy of one).

A Solidity import statement in-scope names an IERC4626 interface file, whether or not the importing contract ends up inheriting it (import-only is still a strong signal of intended conformance, captured distinctly from actual inheritance).

A function carries an explicit `@inheritdoc IERC4626` NatSpec tag -- a direct developer assertion that this function implements the ERC-4626 interface's obligation for that method, independent of whether the containing contract also formally inherits the interface type.

Project documentation (README*, NatSpec @notice/@dev contract-level comments, docs/ directory) explicitly claims ERC-4626 conformance in prose, independent of code structure. A documentation claim alone is sufficient to mark the standard applicable -- claimed-but-nonconforming is itself relevant (see fixture 6 in the discovery test suite), not a reason to skip detection.

supporting.description: The canonical ERC-4626 method signature set. A SINGLE matching signature (e.g. just totalAssets()) is NOT sufficient on its own to classify a contract as ERC-4626 -- per the plan's explicit instruction not to classify on one common function name alone. Used as a supporting signal that raises confidence only when combined with a meaningful subset (discovery.py defines the exact threshold) or co-occurring with a strong signal.

The two ERC-4626-defined events, matched by name AND indexed-parameter shape (both names are common in isolation -- e.g. plain ERC-20-adjacent 'Deposit' events exist elsewhere -- so signature shape, not name alone, is what's checked).

Import path references a known, widely-used ERC-4626 reference implementation from a third-party library (OpenZeppelin, Solmate, Solady). Supporting rather than strong: importing a library file is evidence of intent but the importing contract must still be checked for actual inheritance/usage, not just the import line.

detection_signal_design_note: Every discovery decision in rtf/standards/discovery.py must cite which of these signal_ids fired, with confidence and evidence populated in a StandardDetectionResult -- no undocumented ad hoc pattern matching outside this registered signal set.
